summary: 22 rows reviewed with git archaeology against cm-main (2230 commits). One blocker-level gap found: v2's GP9 lifecycle test (stdin EOF + parent kill) does not cover the OpenCode/host-never-dies case that caused #999/#568, and the only historical fix for that case (idle-shutdown timer, #568) was later reverted (#602) for breaking tools on 12 hosts. v2 docs are silent on how #999 closes, so this is a needs-decision, not closed-by-design. #985 and #1024 are correctly closed by ADR-0002 (confirmed by archaeology). #967 is closed-by-design by ADR-0016 (confirmed: history shows two earlier prose-injection attempts, both later replaced). Rows with no code history in cm-main are policy/process rows (D, C, Q) and are left as-is.

items.ref: TECH-SPEC GP9: 'Lifecycle | stdin EOF, parent kill, on 3 OS | exit < 2 s; no spawn at boot; no chdir | #1100 #982 #953 #1167 #923 #924 #974' — #999 is NOT in GP9's issue list
items.archaeology: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY the underlying bug class is described verbatim in ac11f103 'fix(lifecycle): idle self-shutdown + generalized sibling sweep (#565) (#568)': 'OpenCode/KiloCode open one MCP child per session and per subagent task and never tear them down for the host's lifetime ... ppid never changes (host stays alive), ... stdin EOF was removed in #471'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (quoted): add a 15-min idle self-shutdown timer plus a generalized sibling-sweep regex covering all install shapes, because neither stdin-EOF nor parent-death detection fires for OpenCode. This exact fix was REVERTED four months later by a888cac6 'revert: lifecycle idle-shutdown (#568 + #595) — restore tools on 12 hosts (#602)' because the idle timer broke tool availability on 12 hosts. REGRESSION_RISK: v2's GP9 test only covers 'stdin EOF, parent kill' — the two mechanisms #568's own commit message says do NOT fire for OpenCode. #999 (23 accumulated start.mjs instances) is the same class of bug #568 was written to fix, and GP9 as currently scoped does not test the OpenCode-stays-alive case at all. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: any re-introduction of an idle-shutdown timer needs the full per-adapter test matrix #568 built (tests/lifecycle-cross-adapter.test.ts style, 14 PlatformIds) before it ships, because the revert happened precisely because that coverage was insufficient the first time. If v2 ships GP9 unchanged, #999 is not closed — it is reproduced on every OpenCode/KiloCode-style host that never emits stdin EOF or changes ppid.
items.regressions: BLOCKER: the #568 idle-shutdown fix for this exact bug class was reverted in a888cac6 for breaking 12 hosts; v2's GP9 does not list #999 and only tests stdin-EOF/parent-kill, which is exactly what #568 found insufficient
items.question: GP9 does not cover the host-never-dies case (OpenCode/KiloCode) that caused both #999 and the original #565/#568 fix. Does v2 add an idle-shutdown timer (repeating the #568 approach, with its full per-adapter test matrix this time) or accept unbounded process accumulation on hosts without stdin-EOF/parent-death signals?
items.recommendation: treat as blocker, not closed-by-design: add #999 explicitly to GP9's issue list and specify the idle-shutdown mechanism (with the cross-adapter test matrix #568 used) in TECH-SPEC before sign-off, or explicitly accept the risk in an ADR

items.archaeology: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY e19bf0cc 'feature: add SessionStart hook with XML routing block', then ec53f516 'feature: replace plain-text Task routing block with XML structure' (an earlier prose block replaced by an XML one, same bug class: injected instructional text confusing the host's own classifiers), and 8471820d 'feat(v0.9.18): cross-platform Windows fix, JSON chunking, intent-aware Read guidance (#43)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: get routing guidance in front of the model without a dedicated tool call. REGRESSION_RISK: ADR-0016's mechanism (deny-with-reason, updatedInput, updatedToolOutput) is structurally different — it rewrites the tool call/result rather than injecting a freestanding prose block into the prompt, so the auto-mode-classifier-trips-on-injected-block failure mode #967 reports should not recur. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: any future SessionStart or PreCompact text injection (see #1028, D9) must avoid reintroducing a bare XML/prose block of the kind e19bf0cc and ec53f516 both had to replace.
items.regressions: pattern already shows TWO prior attempts at prose/XML injection, both later replaced — a third attempt (e.g. in D9's SessionStart hint, #1028) should be checked against this history
items.question: none for #967 itself
items.recommendation: closed-by-design for #967; flag the pattern (two prior injected-block rewrites) as a caution for whatever D9's SessionStart hint ends up injecting
